newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA FUEL OIL - MARKET RANGEBOUND IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ASIA FUEL OIL - MARKET RANGEBOUND IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was syeady on Monday in lacklustre trading in the absence of fresh indicators, traders said.
Trading was rangebound as the market was supported at $102.00 per tonne with a seller at just 50 cents above this level.
Fuel oil traded on Friday at $102.50 per tonne.
Traders said market fundamentals are unchanged with no additional demand seen from China where buyers are sidelined in expectation of a price slip once supplies from the Middle East pick up.

But traders said supplies from the Middle East remain limited due to the seasonal summer peak demand there. Also the start up of new Iranian crude unit has not had much impact on market with on-spec cargo largely sold for export to the West, they said.
The National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) started up one of its two 116,000-barrel-per-day unit in late June which is currently operating at 70,000-bpd.
The refinery has yet to produce on-spec diesel or gasoline, they said.
South Korean ports re-opened on Monday after Typhoon Tina passed through the south coast of the peninsular without any major damage.
Industry sources said the oil companies have resumed bunker operations after closing done on Friday.
Despite the closure of the bunker ports in South Korea for two-days, demand in Singapore was thin.
Bunker prices edged down slightly with some 380-cst supplies sold at $104.50 per tonne, 50 cents lower than Friday's selling price.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a tender to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent, 180-centistoke fuel oil for September 11-20 lifting, industry sources said.
The tender closes on August 14 and bids will be valid until August 15. In its last tender, Taiwan sold one cargo at around $100 per tonne on a free-on-board Kaoshiung basis.
